content.text: For digital creators in restricted countries like Nigeria or Kenya, building a store that accepts crypto payments without relying on platforms like Stripe can be a daunting task. However, with the Sovereign Commerce infrastructure, you can deploy a fully operational online store, complete with automatic crypto payment processing and instant product delivery, all while maintaining full data ownership and control. In this guide, we'll walk you through the process of setting up a Supabase-based order database for your digital store, without requiring Stripe or any other centralized payment processing platform.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Unlike traditional e-commerce solutions that rely on centralized payment processors, the Sovereign Commerce infrastructure empowers you to take control of your payment and delivery pipeline. By leveraging GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, you can create a fully custom and scalable solution that adapts to your unique needs. This decoupling from centralized platforms allows you to avoid the risks associated with platform restrictions and payment processing limitations, ensuring a seamless and secure experience for your customers.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital store, you'll need to familiarize yourself with the Sovereign Commerce infrastructure and its various components. This includes understanding how to configure GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage. Additionally, you'll need to set up NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification and configure your payment and delivery pipeline accordingly. By taking the time to understand these components and their integrations, you'll be well-prepared to deploy a robust and scalable digital store.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to configure NOWPayments to work seamlessly with your Supabase-based order database. This involves setting up a webhook to trigger payment confirmation and updating your order storage accordingly. Additionally, you'll need to configure Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 for file delivery, ensuring that your customers receive their digital products instantly upon payment confirmation. By streamlining your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll be able to process transactions efficiently and provide a seamless experience for your customers.
By leveraging the Sovereign Commerce infrastructure, you can decouple from centralized platforms and avoid the risks associated with payment processing limitations.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once your payment and delivery pipeline is set up, you can deploy your digital store and begin processing transactions. To do this, you'll need to deploy Stack 01 using the Sovereign Blueprint, which includes GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments. After deployment, you can test your store on the mainnet, ensuring that everything is working as expected. By going live and processing your first transaction, you'll be able to validate your setup and make any necessary adjustments before scaling your digital store.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your digital store is up and running, you can scale your infrastructure to meet growing demands. This involves configuring additional components, such as SPF/DKIM/DMARC for email deliverability and load balancing for increased traffic. By scaling your infrastructure in a controlled and incremental manner, you'll be able to ensure that your digital store remains performant and secure, even as it grows in popularity.
